rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis uses molecular dynamics tensile loading on a single-crystal FeNiCrMn HEA, while the target applies thermal aging treatments to an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (simulation vs. thermal processing).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis conditions involve vacuum MD simulation at 10–600 K with high strain rates, whereas the target uses aging at 550–750°C in a furnace. The regimes are entirely different (cryogenic-to-moderate temperature simulation vs. intermediate-temperature thermal exposure).
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis mechanism is dislocation nucleation at vacancies and partial-dislocation-mediated plasticity, while the target mechanism involves L12 ordering, APBE elevation, restricted cross-slip, and stress concentration at jagged phase boundaries. These are different classes of embrittlement mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts orientation-dependent yield strength and temperature/rate sensitivity, while the target predicts a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with aging temperature. The properties (yield strength vs. ductility) and the nature of the prediction are entirely different.
